label: an American infantryman of the War of 1812 years, and the pattern before it
note: Gathered 2026-11-07 for T-3451, the 1812 private of the First Infantry (anonymous; Heald's company). None shows the Fort Dearborn garrison or a regular of the First: Krimmel's Philadelphia volunteers (1811-13) near and far, and Ogden's 1888 reconstruction of the 1802-1810 pattern a frontier company may still have worn. A reference set says what a soldier of the time looked like, never what the garrison wore.

pictures.name: krimmel_1813_soldiery
pictures.from: Met open-access image DT1810 (3032 x 3717), crop [1758, 929, 2971, 3605], the two men at the right, at full resolution
pictures.caption: John Lewis Krimmel, Members of the City Troop and Other Philadelphia Soldiery, 1811-ca. 1813, the right-hand men. The Met 42.95.21
pictures.shows: Two volunteers at a metre or two, whole: short blue coats faced orange-red, dark crossbelts crossing on the breast, cartridge box and bayonet, blue pantaloons, black gaiters, bearskin caps.
